high_level_description: This black-and-white photograph captures a moment from 1966, showing Colonel Harland Sanders, the founder of Kentucky Fried Chicken (KFC), opening a new restaurant near Fort Campbell in Nashville. The image is set outside the KFC restaurant, which prominently displays the iconic logo and name "Kentucky Fried Chicken" on its sign. In the foreground, two men are featured. On the left, there is a man wearing a white shirt with a black bow tie and a pocket square. He appears to be smiling and looking towards the right side of the frame.
